takeaway: Anthropic's amended S-1 puts its run-rate revenue at about $81 billion as of Oct 31, the most authoritative AI revenue figure the radar holds, and below an earlier press report of $100B. A fake-repo campaign of about 30 'ai--manus' clones was deleted overnight.

findings.heading: Anthropic files: ~$81B run rate on Oct 31
findings.text: The S-1/A says run-rate revenue was approximately $81 billion as of Oct 31, up $10 billion from Sept 30. It supersedes the $100B (Sept 18) press figure the radar recorded earlier.

findings.heading: A fake 'ai--manus' repo campaign is deleted
findings.text: 36 repos the radar tracked now return HTTP 404, about 30 of them 'ai--manus' clones under random accounts. They carried AI tags, so the radar's term filter could not catch them.

findings.heading: Chrome's agent tooling keeps climbing
findings.text: GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src gained 1,219 stars, to 6,299. ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp gained 790, to 56,458.

findings.heading: Level AI: $20M ARR, ~50% growth
findings.text: On Five9's Q3 call, management said Level AI had stand-alone ARR of about $20 million as of Oct 31, growing about 50% year over year.

findings.heading: Nov 8 forecast: 0.52, 4 of 15 picks right
findings.text: Rank correlation 0.52 over its own top 100, every one scored on growth the radar measured itself; its top 15 held 4 of the real top 15.

caveats: Anthropic's $100B press figure and $81B filed figure both stay in the record; the radar reads the pair as a decline, which it is not.
Fake repos that copy AI tags pass the radar's filters until they are deleted.
Hacker News and npm remain unreachable from the cloud environment.
